data.function: P2 report: Critical line blanking time (V287)
data.ruling: The refutation holds. The refresh figures re-derive. tCONVERT at CT=100 is 1.1 ms typical and 1.21 ms maximum (6.5). Three shunt-only channels give one refresh of 3.3 ms typical and 3.63 ms maximum (7.4.1). SBOS576C gives no minimum conversion time. The hold times the claim builds on these figures do not come from the datasheet. "A single conversion holds its node low for at most 3.63 ms; two consecutive hold it 6.6 ms typ and abort" assumes that the transparent Critical pin stays low from one over-limit conversion of a channel until that same channel's next conversion. It also assumes that the in-limit conversions of the other two channels in between do not release the pin. SBOS576C does not say this. 7.3.2.1 says only that the pin "pulls low if any channel measurement exceeds the limit". Table 8-34 defines CEN=0 only as "Transparent (default)". 9.2.2 and Figure 9-2 show one enabled channel (CH1) and say only that the pin "pulls low after the conversion cycle completes". With three channels enabled, the release point is not stated. The two TI E2E threads (Engineer-to-Engineer, TI's support forum) do not settle it either. In thread 1625525, a TI engineer says the transparent alert "clears" as soon as the shunt voltage drops below the limit. He says nothing about another channel's conversion. In thread 807608, a customer saw Ch.1's critical alert stay active for 50 ms = 6 channels x 8.24 ms, which fits the claim's model. That is one unqualified scope observation, under unstated conditions while he raised the limit, not a maker figure. A TI engineer there says the pin restores "after one conversion", without naming which channel's. Under the verifier's reading, a sustained overcurrent on one channel holds the shared line low for about 1.1 ms in every 3.3 ms. That stays below the 5 ms blanking at every current, so the abort would never fire. The datasheet does not rule that reading out. The figure states an unknown as a fact. It holds only after a bench measurement of the Critical pin with 3 channels enabled and one over the limit, or after TI states the release point. Scope is function: the point is the blanking time's fit to this function's alert timing, not the part's identity or lifecycle.
data.evidence: SBOS576C (revised September 2026), 6.5: tCONVERT at CT bit = 100 is 1.1 ms typical, 1.21 ms maximum; no minimum. 7.4.1: one sequence's time is the sum of the enabled conversion times; 3 shunt-only channels give 3.3 ms typical, 3.63 ms maximum. 7.3.2.1: "The Critical alert pin pulls low if any channel measurement exceeds the limit present in the corresponding-channel critical-alert limit register"; nothing on when it releases. Table 8-34, bit 10 CEN: "0 = Transparent (default) / 1 = Latch enabled"; transparent behaviour not defined further. 9.2.2 and Figure 9-2: one enabled channel (CH1); the pin "pulls low after the conversion cycle completes". E2E 1625525, TI engineer: in transparent mode "As soon as the shunt voltage drops back down below the programmed level, the alert clears" (per signal; other channels not mentioned). E2E 807608, customer: "The Critical flag (Ch.1) remains active for 50ms (6 channels sampled x 8.24ms)"; TI engineer: "the Critical pin should restore automatically after one conversion" (which channel's conversion not stated). The datasheet states no release point with 3 channels enabled. The hold times 3.63 ms max and 6.6 ms typ are an inference. Not measured.
